---
title: "Plotly widget lifecycle"
---

Cards with changing Plotly results create one FigureWidget in a dependency-free
render_widget output. A separate effect updates it through update_figure().
WidgetSlot owns replacement and session-end cleanup. Data, metrics and fullscreen
controls must not cause repeated construction of browser widget models.

Candidate ensemble, duplicates and variable similarity follow this pattern, like
Candidate training, Candidate models and data homogeneity. Metric, member, style, pending/result and fullscreen updates retain the same
widget/view. Rendering is independent of background fitting.

The installed shinywidgets 0.8.2 bridge and its bundled Jupyter model.close()
also have an asynchronous teardown defect. Jupyter deletes model.views before
pending view removals execute; their callbacks still dereference model.views.
The bridge explicitly pre-removes only views with destroy(), while current
anywidget Plotly views expose remove() without destroy(). Its legacy branch also
deletes view.model prematurely. The resulting JavaScript Error object appears as
{} in some console displays; the captured stack dereferences model.views.

widget_lifecycle adds a narrowly versioned compatibility script when shinywidgets
is 0.8.2 and its bundle contains the affected deletion. It leaves the provider's
output binding, manager and comm handlers intact. The script wraps WidgetModel.close
once, restores missing view.model references and retains the view registry until
asynchronous close completes. Repeated closure shares the same pending operation.
Exceptions propagate to the provider's existing reporting; no console filtering is
introduced. Installed site-packages files are not modified. Other versions need
independent verification before extending or removing the workaround.

The earlier full output-binding replacement has been removed. Registering a second
binding/manager after an existing output was displayed could split output rendering
from model-message handling and cause "No model found for id". The regression
creates one output before compatibility setup, inserts another after the first
is displayed, and refreshes both. Both outputs must continue sharing the provider's
single manager. Module installs the guard before card UI construction, including standalone cards.
The small compatibility script is an additional HTMLDependency;
it never replaces the provider dependency or registers a widget output binding.

Browser regressions exercise repeated real widget replacement, explicit closure,
DOM view removal, and deliberate unexpected teardown failure. Candidate ensemble
regressions assert widget identity and absence of browser errors across metric,
member, style, enablement and fullscreen changes. The continuous upstream-progress
regression remains applicable.

Preview-card regressions also cover duplicates, homogeneity and variable similarity
charts across initial display and fullscreen changes.
